_comment: Military balancing. territory: radius of the land an occupied building claims, in the round hex metric of PathFinder.InCircle. Measured from the original maps' owner bytes (edge of the land around the buildings: tower 931, big tower 967, castle 1101 = radius squared), so the values reproduce the original.
_soldiersComment: Homestead's own combat values. damage per hit, one hit every attackSeconds; speed: walking speed as a factor (1 = as everybody); bowmen shoot up to range fields but not at enemies nearer than minRange (they step back first; not from the top of a military building), from military buildings towerRangeFactor times as far. armor: share of every hit a soldier of the type does not take (the rest rounded down, at least 1; pikemen take half). Level 2/3 multiply health and damage by levelBonus.
_doorComment: Attacked military buildings: melee attackers first break the door (as much health as a level-1 soldier of type healthOf). With no enemy within calmRadius fields of the door fight for calmSeconds, the guard goes back in and the door repairs itself evenly, from broken to whole in regenSeconds (half after 15 s); already its first moment of repair takes another hit to break it. fighters: how many melee attackers fit at the door at once (fields next to it; pikemen too, bowmen not at all), per building name, 2 elsewhere.

door._pointsComment: Where a door fight takes place, per people and building, as grid offsets [x, y] from the door: guard = where the defender stands, fighters = where melee attackers fight it (the first 'fighters' of them are used). One step in x is 16 px to the right on screen, one step in y 9 px down and 8 px to the left; lower fields are drawn in front of the building. Buildings missing here (or with a field that is not walkable on the spot) get fields found automatically.

_garrisonCallRadiusComment: Military buildings call only idle soldiers of their player within this many fields of the door; those further away stay where they are.
_hospitalComment: Hospital: its healer calls the weakest wounded own idle soldier (least health left, ties: the nearest; not one holding its position) within callRadius fields of the door to the field in front of it. Whenever wounded own soldiers stand still at the door, the healer comes out, heals the weakest fully in healSeconds and goes back in; after a heal it waits callPauseSeconds before calling the next one (soldiers that come by themselves are healed at once).
_geologistHealthComment: Geologists of other players are fought like soldiers (they do not strike back) and have this much health.
_scoutsComment: Scouts look like a carrier of their own to other players. An enemy soldier outside the buildings within revealRadius fields sees through it; revealed, he stays so while that player sees him (own land, sight of own settlers and buildings, as the fog of war). A computer player grows suspicious of a scout on its land and sends a soldier to look. Only revealed is he fought (health as for geologists, he does not strike back). sight: radius he sees in the fog of war (a settler sees 8). Stealing, he takes the nearest good of somebody else within stealRadius fields, one unit, and walks at loadedSpeed times his speed until he stands still on his own land, where he drops it (also where he dies).
_pioneersComment: Pioneers take land („Land einnehmen“): free land and land of other players no occupied military building of theirs covers, one field after another (the field they stand on and the unwalkable ones around it), each taking claimSeconds; a shore field also takes the free water off it up to waterReach fields out (room for a dock and fishers, no border posts left at the shore); the next field is the nearest such within searchRadius around them (ties: nearest to where they were sent). Fought like geologists (health), they do not strike back.
_buildingSightComment: Fog of war: finished own buildings of these names reveal their surroundings up to this radius; occupied military buildings see militarySightMargin fields beyond their land; every other finished building (houses, storehouses, workshops, …) sees otherBuildingSight fields; construction sites and the land itself see nothing (only settlers outside do).
_warMachinesComment: War machines (Kriegsmaschinen), one kind per people, built in its works: the worker hammers cost (machine) or ammo (one load) together in front of the door, unit by unit, buildSeconds each. A new machine comes with shots, a load fills it up again (the Amazon gong needs none: shots 0). Driven like soldiers at speed, they fire at enemy military buildings only (in range, cooldownSeconds between shots, hitting with hitChance); each hit takes one of the building's hits (buildingHits), the last brings it down, its soldiers walk out alive; a damaged building mends one hit every repairSeconds after the last. Melee soldiers destroy machines (health), bowmen cannot hurt them. Reloading: within reloadDistance of an own works of its kind with a load. Values guessed (the user tunes them against the original): only hitChance and the cooldown were given.
_combatPathRadiusComment: Near the enemy, soldiers plan their way within this radius around everyone standing (own soldiers too).
_combatStrengthComment: Combat strength (Kampfkraft) like the original: on own land a soldier always hits with 100 %. Elsewhere (neutral or enemy land) it starts at startPercent[number of players - 1] (more players: the last value), measured in the original right after the start for 2–8 and 16 players, the others from the fit 292 / (players + 3.8) (1 player: 54 % like the original – pointless without enemies, but a connoisseur would notice); goods lying on the player's own land raise it without limit (200 %: soldiers hit twice as hard away from home – a rich player is pushed to attack). goods: what a unit counts (per people in civilizations: Egyptians get half from gold and double from gems). Each further percent costs what the band of the strength reached so far asks: unitsPerPercent[i] units per point for i·stepPercent to (i+1)·stepPercent % (counted from 0 %, not from the start; the last value goes on), so the same gold buys more from a low start. Measured in the original (1, 2 and 6 players, 2026-10): 1.2 bars per point up to 50 %, then 2.6, 4, 8, 12, and 20 from 90 % on. Two players need 26 bars for 60 %, 146 for 80 %, 466 for 100 %, then 20 per point.
